newsitem.title: DUBAI: Philippines seeks Saudi clemency for death-row maid.
newsitem.headline: Philippines seeks Saudi clemency for death-row maid.

text.p: The Philippines has appealed to Saudi Arabia's King Fahd to reconsider a death sentence passed on a Filipina maid for killing her Saudi female employer, an official said on Tuesday.

The Philippine embassy's acting head of assistance for Filipinos in Saudi Arabia, Dauday Tago, said a Saudi court in February passed the sentence on maid Sarah Dematera. He confirmed a newspaper report saying the execution was being suspended until the victim's children reach the age of 18.

"My ambassador wrote an appeal to the custodian of the two holy mosques (King Fahd)...for retrial or reinvestigation of the case, or the grant of a pardon, or the reduction of the penalty imposed," he told Reuters by telephone from Riyadh.
"We have not yet received a reply, as far as I know."
The Philippines ambassador could not immediately be reached for comment.

Tago said Dematera, 24 years old and from Antipolo near Manila, was tried for murdering her Saudi female employer. She was arrested in November 1992 and the court handed down a death sentence in February 1996, he said.
The execution has been postponed so the victim's children could decide Dematera's fate, the United Arab Emirates Gulf News reported earlier this week.

Saudi Arabia executes drug traffickers, murderers and rapists, mostly by sword, in its implementation of Islamic sharia law. But relatives of a victim can pardon a convicted murderer or accept blood money instead.
The kingdom executed 192 people in 1995 and 28 this year.

"The execution of the punishment has been postponed until the minor children of the deceased reach the age of majority...to determine whether they will forgive or just accept blood money for the crime," he said. He said he did not know their ages.
Tago said that Dematera initially "pleaded innocence". He quoted from what he said was a letter from Dematera to the ambassador in which she asserted that she had been framed.
"...later on in the investigation...she was made to accept the crime with the promise that she will be released," he said. "The initial suspect was the husband of the victim."
"According to the letter of Miss Dematera, she (the victim) was beaten by a masked man with a pipe," Tago told Reuters.
He said Dematera was the only Filipina on death row in Saudi Arabia. The 500,000 Filipinos in the Gulf Arab state make it one of the largest expatriate Filipino communities.
"We are following this very closely," Tago said.
World attention focused on the plight of Asian maids in the Gulf after a United Arab Emirates court in 1995 sentenced Filipina maid Sarah Balabagan to death for stabbing her employer.
Balabagan, whose sentence was later reduced to imprisonment and lashings, said she acted in self defence during an alleged rape. She was released this year.
Maids across the Gulf have alleged abuses ranging from rape to non-payment of salaries, according to embassy officials.
Filipino Vice President Joseph Estrada has asked Saudi Arabia for permission to visit the kingdom to meet Filipino workers and discuss the welfare of his country's community there, Tago said.
He said the time of the visit has not been confirmed and it was not clear whether Estrada would meet Saudi officials.
